result.topic_en: Determining the coefficients A, B, C, D of a series expansion (coefficients 1/4, 1/4·9/16, ...) by two methods of equating coefficients, with a general formula for the n-th equation and derived combinations of the equations.
result.transcription:
11
unde emergunt aequationes
$4A = 1$
$-8A + 16B = A$
$12A - 64B + 64C = A$
$-16A + 160B - 384C + 256D = B$
etc.
atque hinc $A = \frac{1}{4}$, $B = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}$, $C = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}\cdot\frac{25}{36}$, $D = \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{9}{16}\cdot\frac{25}{36}\cdot\frac{49}{64}$,
ut supra: sed legis ratio hinc [-nondum perspicua fit-] operosius dedu-
ceretur: quare methodum sequentem praeferimus. Ex aequatione
$\frac{2t}{1+tt} + A\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^3 + B\left(\frac{2t}{1+tt}\right)^5 + \text{etc.} = 2t(1 + At^4 + Bt^8 \ldots)$ dema-
nant aequationes sequentes:
$1 = 1$ [1]
$0 = 1 - 4A$ [2]
$A = 1 - 12A + 16B$ [3]
$0 = 1 - 24A + 80B - 64C$ [4]
$B = 1 - 40A + 240B - 448C + 256D$ [5]
$0 = 1 - 60A + 560B - 1792C + 2304D - 1024E$ etc. [6]
ubi coëfficientes facile subiiciuntur formulae generali: scilicet aequatio
n ta erit
$M = 1 - 4A \times \frac{n.n-1}{1.2} + 16B \times \frac{n+1.n.n-1.n-2}{1.2.3.4} - 64C \times \frac{n+2.n+1.n.n-1.n-2.n-3}{1.2.3.4.5.6}$
$+ 256D \times \frac{n+3.n+2.n+1.n.n-1.n-2.n-3.n-4}{1.2.3.4.5.6.7.8} - \text{etc.}$
ubi M erit vel $= 0$ (quando n par), vel [-vel-] {+aequalis+} termino $\frac{1}{2}(n+1)^{to}$ seriei
1, A, B, C, D etc. (quando n impar). Iam ex his aequationibus sequentes
nouas deducimus *).

4[3] - [1] | $4A - 1 = 3 - 48A + 64B$

methods.what: Recursive system of linear equations for the series coefficients A, B, C, D
Functional equation under substitution 2t/(1+t^2), equating coefficients
General n-th coefficient equation with binomial-type coefficients
Linear combinations of the equations to derive new ones
